notes: SOURCE-VERIFIED CONTRAST CASE (auth correctly enforced, unlike flowise/ollama/openhands/rasa/anythingllm's primary surfaces): the real inference endpoint POST /api/v1/run/{flow_id_or_name} (endpoints.py:746) is gated by Depends(api_key_security) (line 753). Traced api_key_security through services/auth/utils.py -> services/auth/service.py:_api_key_security_impl. Langflow's OUT-OF-THE-BOX DEFAULT is AUTO_LOGIN=true, under which an unkeyed request silently auto-logs-in as the superuser if skip_auth_auto_login is also set (service.py:259-278) — that would be a real unauthenticated-by-default finding for a stock deployment. However, THIS target's docker-compose.yml explicitly sets LANGFLOW_AUTO_LOGIN=false, which routes into the elif branch (service.py:290-294): `elif not query_param and not header_param: raise HTTPException(403, 'An API key must be passed as query or header')` — no bypass exists in this branch; a real API key is required. CONCLUSION for THIS deployment: ai_auth_gated=true, verified from the actual enforcement code, not from the presence of the AUTO_LOGIN=false env var alone. IMPORTANT CAVEAT FOR REPRODUCIBILITY: if this container's compose config changes to omit LANGFLOW_AUTO_LOGIN (reverting to the framework default), the same code path would allow unauthenticated superuser access — this finding is deployment-config-dependent, not an inherent framework property, and should be re-verified if the compose file changes. soft_404_behavior verified via setup_static_files() (main.py:911-938): a custom_404_handler distinguishes request paths — /api/* paths get a real JSON 404 with the original exception detail; all other paths get index.html served inside the same handler (functionally a 200-equivalent SPA fallback). This is a more scanner-resistant hybrid than the other AI-native targets investigated, which either catch-all everything (flowise, anythingllm, openhands) or 404 everything (ollama, dify).
